text:
Maya (Docs): Pushed a new docs PR to expand the model catalog entry for redwood/mistral-7b: added limits, a tiny benchmark row, compatibility notes for quantized builds, and two SDK examples. Draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/489

infra-bot: PR created (#489) by Maya (Docs) in docs/model-catalog

Owen (ML): Quick bench numbers from our validation cluster (A100-40GB, kv cache warm, single-stream):
```
512 seq: median 7.1 ms/token, ~1400 tok/s
2048 seq: median 10.2 ms/token, ~950 tok/s
peak mem: 512->9.8GB, 2048->17.9GB
```
Also note: quant variant falls back to float kernels on some driver combos; expect +10% latency when that happens. I'll attach CSV to the PR.

Priya (SDK): Added Python + TS snippets in PR comments. Use `model_version` to pin. Small note: response now returns `output_text` for plain text compatibility. Python sample: `client.generate(model="redwood/mistral-7b", model_version="2026-03-01", prompt="Summarize")`

Alex (Product): Please make limits explicit: max context 8192 (recommend customers keep <=4096 for lower latency), hosted soft throttle 150 RPS/model. Add a very small cost bucket row (hosted: medium, dedicated: low, private: variable).

Maya (Docs): Will add "Limits" and a one-line customer guidance in the card. Devon's runtime note about CUDA minimum — what should we list?

Owen (ML): Recommend: CUDA >=11.8 and driver >=528.x. Add compatibility blurb: "Quantized models may execute float kernels on older drivers; if you observe increased latency or OOMs, pin to non-quant model or enable fallback routing."

Priya (SDK): Also fixed a stale link in the README that pointed to `version` param — updated to `model_version` in my small follow-up commit.

Maya (Docs): Great. Leaving PR as draft until CSV and final TS snippet are in. TODOs in PR body: attach bench CSV (Owen), finalize limits table (Alex), add CUDA minimum (Owen), add customer-facing troubleshooting note (Alex).
